experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.asm: xvfdiv.d $xr0, $xr0, $xr2; xvfdiv.d $xr0, $xr0, $xr2; xvpickve2gr.d $r4, $xr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; xvreplgr2vr.d $xr0, $r4
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 2000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 4607182418800017408; xvreplgr2vr.d $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 4607182418800017408; xvreplgr2vr.d $xr2, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0' --asm 'xvfdiv.d $xr0, $xr0, $xr2; xvfdiv.d $xr0, $xr0, $xr2; xvpickve2gr.d $r4, $xr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; xvreplgr2vr.d $xr0, $r4'

latencies.notes: Data-dependent latency. Chain: tested op, then xvpickve2gr.d+and+or+xvreplgr2vr.d to restore the input pattern; the 9-cycle closure is subtracted (calibrated with vadd.b/xvadd.b). Swept 26 operand values including 0, powers of two, max, minnorm, maxsub, minsub, Inf and NaN: latency 8-11 cycles, CPI 4.5-6. The stored experiment uses 1.0. Measured on 2026-11-17 on LA464, core 0.

notes: Latency model: 8 cycles for special operands, 10 when the divisor is a power of two (the stored sample uses 1.0/1.0), 23 for a general divisor, up to +1 with a subnormal operand. The stored experiment runs the division twice, so cycles = (core_cycles - 9.98) / 2. 64-bit vector lanes match the scalar numbers and run in parallel (slowest lane dominates); 32-bit vector lanes cost 2 x scalar - 5. Re-derived with the two-cycle cross-domain calibration: movfr2gr and movgr2fr are 2 cycles each, movgr2frh.w is 3, the flag pair is 7/15, vpickve2gr is 3, xvpickve2gr is 5, and vreplgr2vr/xvreplgr2vr are 2 (3 for the byte and half-word broadcast).
